A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original reasoning-benchmark results, accuracy and timing comparisons, ablations, sensitivity analyses and illustrative model outputs.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, including Tables 1–2 and Figures 3, 5, 7 and 8.

M1.justification: The task-specific prompt search and adaptive reasoning procedure retain Equations (1)–(6), including entropy-based stopping, alternative prompting, Jaccard-based resampling and majority voting. The new reasoning-tree definitions formalize the conceptual analysis without changing the specified method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same six arithmetic, two commonsense and two symbolic datasets. Few-shot evaluation remains on MultiArith and GSM8K, and the AQuA analyses retain their original coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same zero-shot and few-shot prompting baselines, RE2 and Contrastive-CoT comparisons, including their self-consistency variants. The fixed-iteration comparator is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain GPT-3.5-turbo-0125, three self-consistency samples in the main comparisons, identical dataset splits and counts, and the same iteration and sampling sensitivity designs. Temperature notation added to the formal definitions does not report changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The TSP/ARI ablations in Table 1, adaptive-versus-fixed analysis, parameter sensitivity tests, entropy trajectories, reasoning-similarity analysis and appendix case studies are retained. The new reasoning diagram and analogy table are conceptual additions rather than new empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Semantic-entropy estimation from sampled answers remains unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run or seed disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests or another experimental uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Matched numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. Table 1 retains overall accuracies of 79.5% for Zero-Shot-CoT + SC and 83.7% with TSP + ARI; Table 2 retains 85.5% for Few-Shot-CoT + SC and 87.4% with ARI. Empirical plots and appendix results also match.

T1.justification: v4 replaces the initial/optimal answer-cluster formalization with initial reasoning paths and a high-confidence optimal-path set. Definitions 3.3–3.6 and new Appendix A.2 introduce generation distributions, reasoning DAGs, node correctness and iterative path updates. This substantially expands the CoT formal framework; the existing self-training lemma, theorem and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: a self-training/CoT uncertainty-minimization connection, task-specific prompting, adaptive reasoning, and improved accuracy and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: v4 explains how context changes without parameter updates could narrow the answer distribution as correct reasoning subpaths lengthen. It also qualifies optimal reasoning as relative to model capabilities. These refine the mechanism explanation while retaining the existing experimental interpretations and task limitations.

D1.justification: The model identifier, prompt templates, sampling and stopping descriptions, dataset access/split information and code link are retained. The added formal definitions do not disclose new implementation settings or reproducibility resources.

R1.justification: v4 adds Liu et al. (2024) as inspiration for its reasoning-tree definition and removes references to Lanham et al. (2023), Lin et al. (2024), Tur et al. (2005) and Zhang et al. (2022). Related-work discussion is condensed, including removal of the CCoToM passage, without broadly changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Appendix A.2 to Section 2 and is rewritten more concisely. The CoT analysis is reorganized around reasoning paths, the method section becomes Methodology, and affiliations/publication information are updated. Most method, experimental and concluding prose is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2(b) is redrawn as a reasoning DAG with erroneous nodes and corrected paths, with a revised caption. A new analogy table becomes Table 3, subsequent appendix tables are renumbered, and Algorithm 1 is reformatted. Existing empirical displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The reasoning-path definitions, revised Figure 2(b) and new Table 3 make the central analogy more explicit and easier to assess. The gain is modest: the entropy–correctness link remains Assumption 3.7, and Appendix A.13 introduces a small threshold-notation inconsistency between θ and ψ. Overall, clearer exposition provides a limited improvement while the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
